title: Oxidation and reduction
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point requires balancing half-equations in acidic conditions, using H⁺ and H₂O, and no bank point teaches that step; the closest points cover electron loss and gain and half-equations only for atoms and charge, so adding that step would be a new idea rather than a small change.

draft.title: Oxidation and reduction
card: the loss of electrons. The species that loses electrons is oxidised, and its oxidation number goes up.
the gain of electrons. The species that gains electrons is reduced, and its oxidation number goes down.
A half-equation shows one side of a redox reaction, with electrons written as e-. Example: Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e- is oxidation, because electrons are on the product side.

In acidic conditions, balance a half-equation in order: balance atoms other than O and H, add H2O to balance O, add H⁺ to balance H, then add e- to balance charge. Example: MnO4⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e- → Mn²⁺ + 4H2O.
draft.remember: Electrons lost means oxidation. Electrons gained means reduction. Both always happen together.

a.q: In the half-equation Fe³⁺(aq) + e- → Fe²⁺(aq), what happens to the iron?
opts: It is reduced, because it gains an electron
It is oxidised, because it gains an electron
It is reduced, because it loses an electron
It is oxidised, because it loses an electron
a.why: The electron is on the reactant side, so the iron ion gains an electron. Gaining electrons is reduction. Saying it is oxidised is a common mix-up, but oxidation is a loss of electrons.
a.clue: Look at which side of the arrow the electron is on.

b.q: Dichromate is reduced in acidic conditions: Cr2O7²⁻ + 14H⁺ + ?e- → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H2O. How many electrons are needed to balance the charge?
b.why: The left side has a charge of -2 + 14 = +12. The right side has 2 × 3 = +6. Six electrons added to the left give +6 on both sides. They go on the reactant side because this is reduction, a gain of electrons.
b.clue: Add up the charge on each side before adding electrons.

a.best: It is reduced, because it gains an electron

check.summary: No problems found. The definitions, the permanganate half-equation and both answers check out, and the explanations agree with the card.
